items.t: Anthropic Urged to Pause IPO for AI Safety by NYC Comptroller
items.d: Anthropic should pause its initial public offering until it has fully addressed risks around artificial intelligence, according to New York City’s comptroller. A letter from Mark Levine addressed to Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei on Wednesday suggested the Claude developer should instead focus on addressing the unprecedented risks of the technology. Ed Ludlow reports on Bloomberg T

items.t: Inflation hit businesses even harder than consumers last month
items.d: Businesses were hit by inflation last month at levels not seen since late 2022.
items.fullText: Economy Inflation hit businesses even harder than consumers last month Various efforts by the Trump administration to bring down prices have failed to make a meaningful dent in rising costs. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 The PPI report is typically seen as a sign of what’s to come for consumer prices. Justin Sullivan / Getty Images Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 15, 2026, 9:35 AM EDT By Steve Kopack Businesses were hit by inflation last month at levels not seen since late 2022. The latest U.S. wholesale inflation report showed that the prices businesses paid to produce goods in September jumped sharply, to 6.3% on an annual basis. From August, prices overall rose 0.6%, the producer price index report showed. The PPI report is typically seen as a sign of what’s to come for consumer prices, and this one followed a consumer price index report Wednesday that also reflected a jump in prices. Both reports indicate that inflation is back on the rise. But unlike high inflation earlier this year, the current effects of rising prices are distributed broadly across the entire economy — beyond merely those sectors exposed to soaring gas, diesel and jet fuel prices. The consumer and producer price indexes are also the last major inflation readings before voters across the country head to the polls in the midterm elections. At many locations, early voting is already underway. Oil and gas prices have soared ever since the U.S. and Israel launched their war on Iran in February. items.fullText: Dial Up the Cloud: NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 Controls Arrive on GeForce NOW Plus, stream ‘Enshrouded’ 1.0 and ‘Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2’ alongside 10 new games this week. October 15, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Dial in the next gaming session this GFN Thursday. New NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 controls give GeForce NOW members more choice over how supported games look and perform in the cloud, even without the latest hardware. Then, step into the Shroud as Keen Games’ Enshrouded leaves early access with its 1.0 release, or let the bolts fly in Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 . Both are streaming on GeForce NOW at launch. With 10 new games joining the cloud this week, members can put the new controls to work in supported titles and keep playing across supported devices without downloads, installs or expensive hardware upgrades. Fine-Tune the Cloud With DLSS 4.5 Controls More control, more cloud power. NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 controls are now available on GeForce NOW, giving members more choice over how supported games look and perform in the cloud, even without the latest hardware. DLSS Super Resolution sharpens image quality, while Dynamic Multi Frame Generation delivers lower latency and reduces stutter for smoother streaming, and Ray Reconstruction enhances ray-traced visuals. In addition, Ultimate members streaming on GeForce RTX 5080-powered cloud rigs benefit from the maximum available options, including Dynamic Multi Frame Generation up to 4X. From James Bond’s globe-trotting missions in 007 First Light — now with path tracing support — to CONTROL Resonant ’s reality-bending Manhattan and the shadowy scares of Resident Evil Requiem , the controls help fine-tune supported games for image quality, responsiveness or a preferred balance between the two. These new settings are available in the GeForce NOW app under settings, for Windows, macOS, Chrome OS and Steam OS platforms. Members can read here for more details

items.t: Ripple Opens $9 Billion Perp-Trading Boom to Wall Street Clients
items.d: Cryptocurrency firms are increasingly turning to the world of traditional finance for their next leg of growth by positioning themselves as competitors to Wall Street’s entrenched institutional businesses.

items.t: Danish Top Court Backs Jail Term in Landmark AI Child-Abuse Case
items.d: Denmark’s Supreme Court upheld an 18-month prison sentence for a 31-year-old man for possessing and distributing tens of thousands of AI-generated sexual images depicting children, in a closely watched test of how existing child-abuse laws apply to artificial content.

items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Advanced Technology Access for Europe’s Scientific Community Through Open Learning Resources, Collaborations and Compute NVIDIA’s participation in the European Commission’s AI in Science Enablers Initiative deepens its commitment to supporting the pursuit of scientific progress across the region. October 15, 2026 by Rod Evans 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Much of today’s scientific progress begins with computation. But turning accelerated computing’s potential into scientific progress — modeling climate systems, designing molecules, simulating materials and more — depends on more than breakthrough technology. Especially for smaller labs, early-career scientists or science-based startups, the hardest part of research can be everything that comes before the science: assembling tools, finding compute and building the expertise to use both. At the AI in Science Summit in Dublin today, the European Commission launched the AI in Science Enablers Initiative, a shared framework connected to RAISE — the Resource for AI Science in Europe — that brings private-sector support closer to Europe’s research community. items.fullText: 삼성전자, 동남아 가전 테크세미나 개최… 맞춤형 AI 가전·통합 공조 솔루션 선보여 2026/10/15 AI 요약 새로운 뉴스룸 AI 기능을 살펴보세요! 닫기 --> AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 삼성전자가 14일 베트남 하노이에서 동남아 가전 테크세미나 ‘더 브리프(The Brief)’를 열고, 현지 사용자의 라이프스타일에 최적화된 AI 가전과 B2B 솔루션을 선보였다. 이번 행사는 지난 8월 개관한 삼성 ‘비즈니스 익스피리언스 스튜디오 (Business Experience Studio, 이하 BES)’에서 진행됐다. 하노이 PVI 타워에 위치한 베트남 BES는 삼성전자의 다양한 제품과 솔루션을 상업시설 콘셉트로 구현한 전시공간이다. 행사에는 태국, 베트남, 싱가포르 등 동남아 국가의 주요 미디어와 인플루언서들이 참석했다. AI 기반 푸드 경험부터 원격 케어까지…차별화된 AI 홈 경험 제공 삼성전자는 가전이 사용자의 라이프스타일과 상황을 이해하고 이에 맞춰 기기를 제어하거나 솔루션을 제안하는 다양한 AI 홈 경험을 소개했다. 특히 냉장고에 탑재된 카메라 기반으로 식재료를 효율적으로 보관·관리할 수 있도록 돕는 ‘AI 비전’ 기능을 시연했다. 사용자는 ‘AI 비전’을 통해 식재료의 입출고 현황을 실시간으로 확인할 수 있다. 자주 사용하는 식재료는 자동으로 데이터베이스에 저장되고 냉장고는 이 정보를 토대로 구매가 필요한 식재료를 알려준다. 이외에도 ▲한 주간의 식재료 사용을 분석해서 리포트 형태로 제공하는 ‘푸드노트(Food Note)’ ▲냉장고 속 식재료를 기반으로 맞춤 레시피를 추천하는 ‘오늘 뭐 먹지?(What’s for Today?)’ 등 다양한 기능을 제공한다. 삼성전자는 ▲전문 상담사가 원격으로 기기의 상태를 정밀하게 분석하고 적절한 조치 방법을 안내해 주는 ‘가전제품 원격지원(HRM)’ ▲와이파이 탑재 제품 대상으로 지원하는 최대 7년간 무상 소프트웨어 업그레이드 등 차별화된 제품 케어 서비스도 소개했다. 주거공간부터 상업시설까지 아우르는 통합 공조 솔루션 선보여 삼성전자는 고온 다습한 동남아 기후와 현지 사용 환경을 반영해 주거공간과 상업시설까지 다양한 공간에 최적화된 냉방 경험을 제공하는 공조 솔루션도 선보였다. 주거용 제품으로는 사용자의 생활 패턴과 공간 환경에 맞춰 냉기 흐름을 제어하는 ‘비스포크 AI 무풍콤보 프로 벽걸이’ 에어컨을 소개했다. 이 제품은 공간을 구분해 냉기 방향을 섬세하게 제어하는 ‘모션 블레이드’와 사용자의 위치·활동량·부재 등을 감지하는 ‘모션 레이더 센서’를 갖춰 사용자의 취향과 환경에 최적화된 냉방을 제공한다. B2B 전용 제품으로는 호텔, 사무실 등 대형 건물에 적용할 수 있는 시스템에어컨 실외기 ‘DVM S2’와 실내기 ‘무풍 1WAY·4WAY 천장형 카세트’를 전시했다. 또 에어컨과 다양한 IoT 기기들을 하나의 플랫폼에 연결하고 다수의 사업장의 기기 상태와 에너지 사용량 등을 한 눈에 관리할 수 있는 B2B 연결·통합 제어 플랫폼 ‘스마트싱스 프로’를 시연했다. 삼성전자 DA사업부 이상직 부사장은 “삼성전자의 차별화된 AI 기술과 연결성을 기반으로 동남아 고객과 B2B 파트너 모두에게 실질적인 가치와 편의를 제공할 것 “이라고 말했다. ▲ 삼성전자가 14일 베트남 하노이에서 열린 삼성 동남아 가전 테크세미나 ‘더 브리프’에서 냉장고에 탑재된 카메라 기반으로 식재료를 효율적으로 보관·관리할 수 있도록 돕는 ‘AI 비전’ 기능을 시연했다. ▲ 삼성전자가 14일 베트남 하노이에서 열린 삼성 동남아 가전 테크세미나 ‘더 브리프’에서 사용자의 생활 패턴과 공간 환경에 맞춰

items.fullText: 삼성전자, ‘실리콘밸리 미래 통신 서밋 2026’ 개최 2026/10/15 AI 요약 새로운 뉴스룸 AI 기능을 살펴보세요! 닫기 --> AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 삼성전자가 현지시간 14일부터 15일까지 미국 실리콘밸리 마운틴뷰에서 글로벌 통신 업계 파트너들과 차세대 네트워크의 미래를 논의하는 자리를 마련한다. 삼성전자는 14일에 ‘파트너 데이(Partner Day)’를 진행했고, 15일에는 ‘실리콘밸리 미래 통신 서밋 2026(Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit 2026)’을 개최한다. ▲ 14일(현지시간) 미국 실리콘밸리 마운틴뷰에서 진행된 ‘파트너 데이’ 행사 전경. 이번 행사에는 주요 이동통신사∙제조사∙정부 기관∙학계 리더 등 100여 명의 통신 전문가들이 참석해 AI와 다가올 6G 시대 소프트웨어 기반의 네트워크 진화 방향과 통신 산업의 가치 창출을 위한 생태계 협력 방안을 논의한다. 또한, 삼성전자는 ‘AI 내재형 6G 네트워크’ 기술 개발 성과 등을 선보인다. AI 시대의 네트워크 가치 창출을 위한 글로벌 협력 14일 파트너 데이 참석자들은 AI기반 통신산업의 변화에 대응하기 위한 소프트웨어 기반 네트워크 전략과 생태계 차원의 협력 방안을 논의했다. 삼성전자는 기조연설을 통해 AI가 애플리케이션과 서비스를 넘어 인프라 전반을 변화시키면서, 100여 년간 이어진 통신 네트워크도 구조적으로 재편되고 있다고 설명했다. 특히, AI와 가상화를 융합한 차세대 네트워크는 기존의 한계를 넘어 인류가 상상해 온 새로운 방식의 커뮤니케이션을 실현하는 핵심 동력이 될 것이라고 강조했다. ▲ 14일(현지시간) 미국 실리콘밸리 마운틴뷰에서 진행된 ‘파트너 데이’에서 삼성전자 네트워크사업부장 김우준 사장이 기조연설을 하고 있다. 이후, 통신 업계의 집단지성을 모아 AI 시대 네트워크 진화 전략과 방향을 본격적으로 논의하는 시간을 가졌다. 패널 세션에서는 통신 사업자들이 AI 기반 미래 네트워크의 요구사항과 청사진을 공유하고, 제조사들은 AI와 가상화 네트워크 상용화 과정에서 축적한 경험을 나누며 통신 생태계의 지속적인 발전 방향을 논의했다. 또, 단순한 연결 서비스를 넘어 새로운 네트워크 기반 신규 서비스를 발굴해 새로운 사업 기회로 연결하기 위한 방안을 다각도로 모색했다. 삼성전자 네트워크사업부 전략마케팅팀장 박정호 부사장은 “AI 시대의 네트워크는 쏟아지는 신규 서비스의 다양한 요구를 읽고, 가상화를 기반으로 유연하게 변화하며 최적의 답을 제시하는 지능형 인프라로 진화하고 있다”며, “삼성전자는 글로벌 파트너들과 함께 가상화 네트워크의 대규모 상용화를 성공적으로 이뤄왔다. 여기에 앞선 AI 기술을 더해 통신 인프라를 새로운 성장 엔진으로 발전시키고, 업계가 함께 도약하는 길을 앞장서 열어 나가겠다”고 말했다. AI가 불러올 무선 통신의 혁신… 네트워크의 혁신과 확장 15일 개최되는 ‘실리콘밸리 미래 통신 서밋 2026’은 ▲AI 내재형 6G 네트워크(AI-Native 6G Networks) ▲위성통신 기반 6G 커버리지 확장(Taking 6G to Space With NTN) ▲현실과 가상 세계를 잇는 초연결(Connecting the Physical and Digital Worlds) 등 총 3개 세션으로 운영되며, 참가자들은 패널 토의를 통해 자유롭게 질의하고 토론하는 시간을 가진다. ‘AI 내재형 6G 네트워크’ 세션에서는 AI를 통신망 성능과 운영효율 혁신의 핵심 기술로 삼아, 6G 네트워크의 지능형 인프라 진화를 위한 기술적 과제와 협력 방안이 논의된다. ‘위성통신 기반 6G 커버리지 확장’ 세션에서는 저궤도 위성군집의 현황과 미래 전망을 살펴보고 우주 통신의 기술적 장벽과 그 해법으로서의 위성 통신에 대해 토론

Ricursive Intelligence is betting on AI-designed chips to help solve the compute crisis
items.d: The founders detailed how their startup is developing AI that can design chips, learn from each iteration, and improve subsequent designs, all with the goal of automating and accelerating the chip design process.
items.fullText: Ricursive Intelligence founders Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini believe more efficient AI chip design could help solve the compute crisis. The founders took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Wednesday to detail how their startup is developing AI that can design chips, learn from each iteration, and improve subsequent designs, all with the goal of automating and accelerating the chip design process. “There is this understanding that in the next five years we are going to have at least 10,000x more demand for compute, and that’s somewhat potentially conservative,” Goldie said on stage. “So we don’t want to build 10,000 times more data centers. We think that we need to help by making chips that are more efficient, that use the bandwidth in those data centers more efficiently, that use the wafers and fabs more efficiently, because even if we make [data centers] in space or something, I don’t know, you won’t see the sun anymore.” While some may be scared by the thought of AI designing its own chips, Goldie argues that letting AI handle chip design will allow humans to focus on developing applications and exploring new possibilities that can expand what they can accomplish with computing. Image Credits: Kimberly White/Getty Images for TechCrunch “I think the way everything is shifting is that humans bring their great ideas and creative thoughts, and execution is handled by AI,” Goldie said. “And this is happening in chip design, software development, and other places. And that’s something that recursive does for chip design.” The founders say AI is challenging traditional chip design methods by discovering unconventional layouts that can outperform traditional ones. For example, AlphaChip, the AI system the founders previously developed, produced a circular, “donut-shaped” arrangement of chip components that initially surprised engineers but ultimately proved to be successful. items.t: Flock CEO defends surveillance technology amid national backlash: ‘We shouldn’t pause progress’
items.d: At TechCrunch Disrupt, Flock CEO Garrett Langley defended his company's surveillance technology despite growing privacy concerns, arguing that its crime-fighting benefits outweigh the risks of abuse.
items.fullText: Flock’s founder and CEO Garrett Langley doesn’t think the risks of introducing surveillance technology at scale outweigh the rewards. “If we want to live in a society where, if you commit a crime, you have a higher probability of being held accountable, we shouldn’t pause progress,” Langley said, speaking onstage during a panel at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 in San Francisco on Wednesday. During the interview, the controversial founder of the surveillance maker of license plate cameras and other recording devices deflected hard questions about the criticism Flock now faces — which has since led to canceled contracts and even layoffs . Instead, Langley tended to respond to questions with anecdotes from conversations with police chiefs and city leaders across the United States, and tales of the supposed numerous crimes Flock has solved, rather than offer tangible solutions to people’s concerns. In doing so, Langley positioned Flock as an advance in technology that was somewhat inevitable. He stressed that if people wanted to live in a better society — that is, one with reduced crime — they would have to offer up their privacy in return. A similar argument about the trade-offs and rewards could be made for AI, which is marketed to the public as vastly improving our lives, automating tedious tasks, and making things more convenient. The flip side is the cost of sharing everything about ourselves with the makers of the AI agents themselves — and the possibility of the destruction of humanity , according to some. It’s no surprise that the AI backlash shares some overlap with Flock. Much like AI, Flock is a technology that some feel has been forced upon the public without their consent. For Langley, this is just the nature of progress, he explained. “Technology, at its core, in its definition, is just doing things better. items.t: Ambrosia Energy will build a 10 GWh factory in Texas to make batteries for off-grid data centers
items.d: Startup Ambrosia Energy will build a massive factory to crank out batteries to augment solar panels, creating a round-the-clock clean power plant.
items.fullText: Ambrosia Energy has begun work on a massive, 10 gigawatt-hour battery factory near Austin, Texas, co-founder and CEO Ben Longmier announced onstage Tuesday at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco. “That allows us to build about a 300 megawatt power plant per year out at our field sites,” he said. The factory will occupy 150,000 square feet, and Longmier said that Ambrosia plans to reach full production in two to three years. The startup emerged from stealth in June to build power plants for data centers at a cost of $100 per megawatt hour. Longmier and his co-founder, Sara Spangelo, had settled on solar plus batteries as the cheapest option that’s the fastest to deploy. Solar panels power the load during the day and charge the batteries, which discharge at night and on cloudy days to keep the data center operating round the clock. Longmier and Spangelo previously founded the satellite constellation startup Swarm, which they sold to SpaceX. Ambrosia is also beginning work on its first commercial power plant in West Texas later this year, Longmier said. The facility will pair 300 megawatts of solar panels with 660 megawatt-hours of batteries to deliver 30 megawatts of continuous power, with a goal of 99.3% uptime. Even with “overbuilding” solar and batteries to deliver continuous uptime, Longmier said the company can be profitable at $100 per megawatt-hour, making it competitive with natural gas turbines that many hyperscalers are planning to use to power their data centers. Sections of Ambrosia’s first pilot-scale power plant have been operating continuously for more than 100 days, Longmier said. The pilot is capable of generating 200 kilowatts of electricity 24/7. To hit its cost targets, Ambrosia has been finding ways to simplify its components, including solar mounts and battery packs. items.t: Ukraine accuses SpaceX of restricting Starlink, disrupting military amid Trump pressure
items.d: Ukrainian officials and military units accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of throttling a technology at the heart of their battlefield communications and drone operations.
items.fullText: War in Ukraine Ukraine says new Starlink restrictions disrupt military as it reels from intel gaps and Trump clash Ukrainian officials and military units accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of throttling a technology at the heart of their battlefield communications and drone operations. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Zelenskyy slams Trump over deal for Russian diesel 01:32 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 14, 2026, 8:51 AM EDT / Updated Oct. 14, 2026, 3:55 PM EDT By Abigail Williams , Dan De Luce , Gabe Gutierrez , Yuliya Talmazan and Jane Lytvynenko Ukraine has accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of undermining its ability to defend itself by limiting Starlink internet services as it reeled from intense Russian ballistic missile attacks that it said came without the usual warning from allies. Musk put the responsibility for the restrictions on President Donald Trump’s shoulders on social media , saying the military version of Starlink, called Starshield, is owned and controlled by the U.S. government. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” Musk said. A spokesperson for President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NBC News that the limitations remained in place late Wednesday. Facing pressure from Trump to halt strikes on Russia’s energy industry, Kyiv and its backers have worried that Washington could cut off battlefield support to try to force it into concessions at the negotiating table. Ukrainian officials and their European partners were already scrambling to understand the status of U.S. intelligence-sharing after the lack of alert ahead of two Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv this week, two Ukrainian and two European officials told NBC News. Ukrainian firefighters extinguish a blaze at the site of a Russian missile strike at an apartment building in Kyiv on Wednesday amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces New Investments in the UK Startup Ecosystem UK organizations across healthcare, finance, local government and climate science are putting NVIDIA AI to work. October 13, 2026 by Anthony Hills 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Across industries, the U.K. is putting the full stack to work. T he scale of deployment is growing fast, from enterprises transforming their businesses to startups solving some of the planet’s hardest problems. NVIDIA is putting that principle into practice, including through a five-year, $250 million compute commitment to strengthen the U.K.’s agentic safety and security research. NVIDIA’s Investments in the UK NVIDIA has been investing in the U.K. startup ecosystem, supporting companies including Basecamp Research , Ineffable Intelligence , Synthesia , Wayve and many more. Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Boltz , Foresight , Hiverge, Prima Mente and Riverlane . Boltz , a London-based AI startup founded by MIT researchers, builds biomolecular models and AI agents that help scientists predict molecular structures and interactions, and design potential new medicines. Foresight, a London-based startup, helps owners of major infrastructure projects, including hyperscale data centers, predict completion dates, mitigate risks and accelerate time to revenue. Hiverge , a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning. Prima Mente , a London-based AI biology startup, focuses on building biological foundation models to decode complex diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets, starting with Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and ALS.
